content:
#41222 removes redundant imports of the following form: Suppose A import B and C and B (transitively) imports C; then C can be removed from the imports of A.

About 15% of all imports (translates to 4k lines) can be removed this way. The PR achieves a small performance improvement.

I would like to do more import decreasing PRs in this direction (without lake shake, which still experiences some issues, see i.e. #40961) and this PR is kind of a prerequisite for that. #41222 is also vulnerable to merge conflicts, so I would greatly appreciate a review. :)

Are you sure it isn't too early to perform this change? What if it turns out B can import C privately instead of publically? Your PR would be removing the import and we would have to add it back later

I mean sure, so do you think it would be preferable to first see what imports can be changed to private imports across Mathlib (idk if this has been done before en masse)?
Since I dont think anyone is actively unexposing definitions / changing some into private, that seems like the only relevant consideration right now.

Thinking about this again, I don't think that possible public imports that could be private should stall this; since mathlib (rightly) barely uses import all, private imports are almost never imported transitively.

So any PR changing many public imports to private would need to re-add tons of imports back one way or the other and the effect if #41222 has been merged at that point probably won't make a huge difference in relative terms.

Not too long ago I've heard the opinion of other reviewers that this kind of import reduction isn't desireable. I think the main argument was that there isn't really much to gain from doing so. Has there been any change on that assessment?

This has been way before the module system though. I think working out a plan how mathlib can make more use of the module system might have a bigger impact, wouldn't it?

Recently some PRs reducing imports have been merged without much discussion (i.e. #40832, #40548 or #39610) as long as they dont hurt performance.

Right now mathlib isnt making much use of the module system (about 94% of all imports are public imports and not many defs are unexposed when they could be). Additionally, 2k files dont have imports sorted alphabetically and sorting them would actually break some files (i.e. due to simp normal form changing).

I think it would be desirable to bring mathlib to a state where imports are private when they can be (though that requires another discussion), all files have ordered imports and each file only imports what it actually needs.
This ought to improve performance (though probably not by a lot) and be a bit more maintainable and transparent. For example, in the course of my PR I discovered some instance causing big slowdowns. Through the module system, we now indeed have the tooling to import much more organised.
(And again #41222 is a somewhat easy first step towards that goal :))

Felix Pernegger said:

Thinking about this again, I don't think that possible public imports that could be private should stall this; since mathlib (rightly) barely uses import all, private imports are almost never imported transitively.

So any PR changing many public imports to private would need to re-add tons of imports back one way or the other and the effect if #41222 has been merged at that point probably won't make a huge difference in relative terms.

Do you mean "privatisable imports" rather than "private imports "? If so, I see your argument, but I do not think it is strong enough for us to go forward with your PR, because it might be that 90% of your PR's diff is unnecessary, even if that's only 5% of the hypothetical diff making all privatisable imports private.
